skill.name: vaex
skill.description: Guide Vaex workflows for loading, transforming, aggregating, visualizing, and modeling tabular datasets that exceed available memory.
skill.summary: Analyze out-of-core tabular data with efficient Vaex patterns.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, benign Vaex terminology, and documented memory mapping. Confirmed risks include public server binding, inline cloud credentials, and unchecked file deletion; semantic review also found plaintext WebSocket guidance and an inline database password. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The server example exposes a dataset service on all interfaces and documents a plaintext remote connection.
remediation.suggestion: Bind to loopback by default, require authentication and firewall controls, and document TLS-protected remote connections.

remediation.issue: The archive example deletes the original file without validating the compressed copy or requesting confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the archive, request explicit deletion approval, and retain or move the original until recovery is confirmed.

remediation.issue: Cloud and database examples place credential placeholders directly in source text.
remediation.suggestion: Use credential providers or secret managers, and avoid literal keys or passwords inside source code and connection strings.

content.value_statement: Large tabular datasets can exceed memory and make standard DataFrame workflows slow. This skill guides efficient Vaex loading, processing, aggregation, visualization, and machine learning.
actual_capabilities: Open and convert CSV, HDF5, Arrow, Parquet, and FITS datasets with Vaex.
Build lazy filters, expressions, virtual columns, joins, and grouped aggregations.
Batch delayed statistics and optimize memory use for out-of-core processing.
Create histograms, heatmaps, selections, subplots, and interactive visualizations.
Prepare scalable features and connect Vaex workflows with common machine learning libraries.
Guide local, cloud, database, and remote dataset input and output workflows.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples; it does not bundle Vaex or execute analysis independently.
No datasets, cloud accounts, database connections, or credentials are included.
Remote services and destructive file operations require separate security review and user approval.
API compatibility and performance depend on the installed Vaex version, storage format, and environment.

use_cases.title: Explore datasets beyond memory
use_cases.description: Inspect columns, calculate statistics, and filter very large tables without loading every row into memory.

use_cases.title: Build efficient data pipelines
use_cases.description: Convert inefficient source formats, create lazy transformations, and export reusable columnar datasets.

use_cases.title: Prepare large machine learning features
use_cases.description: Scale, encode, and transform large feature tables before integration with supported model libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a large dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [file path] with Vaex. List columns and types, then summarize numeric fields without loading the entire dataset into memory.

prompt_templates.title: Create lazy transformations
prompt_templates.prompt: Filter [dataset] using [condition]. Add virtual columns for [calculations], then aggregate [metrics] by [grouping columns].

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an existing pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Vaex workflow for memory and performance problems. Recommend lazy expressions, delayed calculations, suitable formats, and safe checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Vaex pipeline for [data volume and source]. Include validation, transformations, storage, recovery, access controls, and performance monitoring.

output_examples.input: Inspect a 200 GB HDF5 dataset containing transaction records.
output: Dataset overview with row count, column names, types, and missing-value counts.
Lazy summary plan for transaction amounts, dates, and customer categories.
Warnings for operations that would materialize the complete dataset.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow workflow that calculates ten independent statistics.
output: Batch the statistics as delayed operations to reduce repeated dataset scans.
Keep derived fields virtual until repeated use or export justifies materialization.
Store checkpoints in HDF5 or Arrow instead of repeatedly parsing CSV.

output_examples.input: Plan a heatmap for billions of coordinate records.
output_examples.output: Use Vaex grid aggregation across all rows, set practical axis limits, and choose a resolution that balances detail with response time.

best_practices: Prefer HDF5, Arrow, or Parquet for repeated work with large datasets.
Keep transformations lazy and batch independent calculations when possible.
Validate output files before replacing or deleting original data.
anti_patterns: Do not convert complete large datasets to pandas or NumPy without a memory estimate.
Do not expose remote dataset servers without authentication, network restrictions, and encrypted transport.
Do not place literal cloud credentials in source code, prompts, notebooks, or shared output.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It guides Vaex workflows for tabular datasets that are too large for conventional in-memory DataFrame processing.

faq.question: Which file formats are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover CSV, HDF5, Arrow, Parquet, FITS, cloud object paths, and several export workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill install Vaex?
faq.answer: No. Vaex and any optional storage, plotting, database, or machine learning dependencies must already be installed.

faq.question: Can it work with cloud data?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure paths, but users must configure access securely.

faq.question: Does it support machine learning?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents feature transformers and integrations with several external machine learning libraries.

faq.question: How should remote Vaex access be secured?
faq.answer: Use restricted network bindings, authentication, firewall rules, and encrypted transport appropriate for the deployment.
